children: Portugal expects to end this year with a balanced budget despite a first-half surplus of 0.5% of GDP, the National Statistics Institute (INE) said on Wednesday in its twice-yearly fiscal data submission to Eurostat.

The government said last week the country could post a small surplus in 2026, which would mark a fourth consecutive year in surplus, but the INE forecast reiterated the government's original projection of no deficit or surplus. Last year, Portugal reported a budget surplus of 0.7% of GDP.
The INE also projected the debt-to-GDP ratio would decline to 87.5% by the end of 2026 from 89.2% last year.
